optionA_DynamicMVT.name: Dynamic MVT via Fastify + PostGIS (ST_AsMVT)
optionA_DynamicMVT.latency: Moderate (50-250ms cold execution depending on complexity and index)
optionA_DynamicMVT.databaseLoad: High (every unique pan/zoom tile runs SQL spatial query unless cached at API/edge)
optionA_DynamicMVT.apiLoad: High (Fastify serializes and compresses tile buffers per request)
optionA_DynamicMVT.cacheability: High at edge if tiles are version-keyed, but low during cold navigation
optionA_DynamicMVT.coldCacheBehavior: Noticeable latency spikes on first visits to dense geographic regions
optionA_DynamicMVT.operationalComplexity: Moderate (relies on existing Fastify backend and PostGIS database)
optionA_DynamicMVT.storageRequirements: Minimal (only PostGIS table storage; zero pre-generated tile files)
optionA_DynamicMVT.invalidationStrategy: Automatic when cache keys include dataset_version_id or entity updated_at
optionA_DynamicMVT.geographyVersionHandling: Excellent (parameters can filter any valid_from/valid_to or version_id on the fly)
optionA_DynamicMVT.provenanceSupport: Direct (reads directly from governed database columns)
optionA_DynamicMVT.mobilePerformance: Excellent once tiles arrive (hardware-accelerated MapLibre rendering)
optionA_DynamicMVT.nationwideScaling: Poor under sudden nationwide load spikes without massive database replicas
optionA_DynamicMVT.failureModes: Database pool exhaustion, query timeouts on unindexed or complex geometry intersections
optionA_DynamicMVT.qualitativeCost: High database compute costs (CPU/RAM scaling required on PostgreSQL)

optionB_PregeneratedMVT.name: Pre-Generated Versioned MVT Directory / S3 Artifacts Behind CDN
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.latency: Very Low (15-50ms at edge PoP, zero database involvement)
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.databaseLoad: Zero during runtime serving; high burst during batch build process
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.apiLoad: Zero (served directly from object storage / static web origin via CDN)
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.cacheability: Maximum (files are immutable, content-addressed, cached permanently)
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.coldCacheBehavior: Fast (edge CDN pulls single static tile from object storage, ~50-80ms once)
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.operationalComplexity: High (requires batch tile generation pipeline, tile storage management, build orchestration)
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.storageRequirements: High (millions of small individual .mvt files across zoom levels z0-z14)
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.invalidationStrategy: Trivial (new versions are written to new content-addressed path; old never mutated)
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.geographyVersionHandling: Good, but requires separate pre-generated tile tree per statutory version
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.provenanceSupport: Baked at build time (immutable metadata in tile properties)
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.historicalGeographySupport: Requires pre-generating tiles for each historical regime; combinatorial storage growth
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.nationwideScaling: Virtually infinite at edge CDN (100k+ concurrent users with zero database load)
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.failureModes: Missing tile files (404), stale CDN caches if cache keys are misconfigured
optionB_PregeneratedMVT.qualitativeCost: Low database compute; moderate object storage file-count and CDN bandwidth costs

optionC_PMTiles.name: Single-File PMTiles Archive on Object Storage with HTTP Range Requests
optionC_PMTiles.latency: Very Low to Low (20-70ms; 2 roundtrips for initial header/directory lookup, 1 for cached leaf)
optionC_PMTiles.databaseLoad: Zero during runtime serving; batch build only
optionC_PMTiles.apiLoad: Zero (client directly fetches byte ranges from CDN / object storage, or lightweight proxy)
optionC_PMTiles.cacheability: High (range requests are cacheable by modern CDNs that support 206 Partial Content)
optionC_PMTiles.coldCacheBehavior: Moderate (first tile in an area requires reading PMTiles directory header)
optionC_PMTiles.operationalComplexity: Moderate (single archive file per state/country/regime instead of millions of small files)
optionC_PMTiles.storageRequirements: Low to Moderate (highly optimized archive format, deduplicates identical tiles)
optionC_PMTiles.invalidationStrategy: Atomic (uploading a new .pmtiles file replaces the entire archive instantly)
optionC_PMTiles.geographyVersionHandling: Clean (one PMTiles archive per dataset_version_id or statutory regime)
optionC_PMTiles.provenanceSupport: Baked at archive creation time with root metadata header
optionC_PMTiles.historicalGeographySupport: Clean (one static archive per historical regime, loaded on demand)
optionC_PMTiles.mobilePerformance: Excellent (MapLibre native integration via maplibre-react-native / protocol handler)
optionC_PMTiles.nationwideScaling: Excellent (scales with object storage read bandwidth and edge CDN range caching)
optionC_PMTiles.failureModes: CDN edge failing to handle HTTP 206 Range requests; corrupt archive header
optionC_PMTiles.qualitativeCost: Lowest storage and compute cost; pay only for S3 storage and egress

optionD_HybridArchitecture.name: Governed Multi-Tier Hybrid (PostGIS Master + Pre-Rendered PMTiles/MVT for Maps + Dynamic Fastify for Spatial Queries)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.latency: Optimal (<30ms visual map rendering from edge; <80ms for dynamic spatial queries)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.databaseLoad: Low (database handles only point-locate, search, and detail queries; zero tile load)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.apiLoad: Low (Fastify handles business logic, auth, and spatial queries; does not stream millions of tiles)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.cacheability: Optimal (visual tiles immutable; query endpoints use short TTL + SWR)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.operationalComplexity: Moderate (controlled build job for PMTiles/MVT upon dataset ingestion; standard API for queries)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.storageRequirements: Moderate (canonical DB tables + compressed PMTiles archives)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.invalidationStrategy: Content-addressed versions and clear separation between static tiles and dynamic queries
optionD_HybridArchitecture.geographyVersionHandling: Comprehensive (handles Current, Historical, Explicit Version, and Scenarios)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.provenanceSupport: 100% compliant with W012 (provenance anchored in DB and referenced in tile headers)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.historicalGeographySupport: Full (historical archives for rendering + historical DB queries for audit)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.mobilePerformance: Maximum (native vector tiles in MapLibre + lightweight JSON for point queries)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.nationwideScaling: Unbounded (scales to all of India without database bottlenecks)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.failureModes: Isolated (if tile CDN is degraded, point queries still work; if API is degraded, cached map still renders)
optionD_HybridArchitecture.qualitativeCost: Balanced and cost-efficient (minimizes high-cost DB compute, leverages low-cost CDN/storage)

regimeA_Current.description: Default active statutory geography currently in legal effect
regimeA_Current.selectionCriteria: is_current = true AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > CURRENT_DATE) AND temporal_classification != 'scenario'
regimeA_Current.fallbackBehavior: Fail-closed (returns 404 / empty if no current version exists; never substitutes historical or scenario)

regimeB_Historical.description: Statutory geography as it legally existed on a specific historical date
regimeB_Historical.selectionCriteria: valid_from <= as_of_date AND (valid_to > as_of_date OR valid_to IS NULL) AND temporal_classification = 'historical_statutory_baseline'
regimeB_Historical.fallbackBehavior: Fail-closed (returns 404 / empty if entity was not yet formed or already dissolved at as_of_date)

regimeC_ExplicitVersion.description: Direct fetch of a specific immutable version record by UUID or version code
regimeC_ExplicitVersion.fallbackBehavior: Strict 404 if record does not exist

regimeD_FutureRegime.description: Statutorily enacted future geography regime not yet in active effect (e.g. pending delimitation)
regimeD_FutureRegime.selectionCriteria: delimitation_regime_id = :regime_id AND valid_from > CURRENT_DATE AND is_current = false
regimeD_FutureRegime.fallbackBehavior: Explicitly labelled as FUTURE_ENACTED; never mixed with active current geography

regimeE_Scenario.description: Hypothetical simulation or draft boundary proposal
regimeE_Scenario.fallbackBehavior: Strictly quarantined; inaccessible via standard public endpoints; requires dedicated scenario routes

tier1_TileFeatureProperties.purpose: Minimal properties embedded in every binary vector tile feature (bandwidth-optimized)
tier1_TileFeatureProperties.rationale: Keeps tile payload under 50-80 KB while preserving client rendering, filtering, and status display

tier2_DetailedMetadataPayload.purpose: Comprehensive governance metadata fetched lazily on entity tap/click via API endpoint
tier2_DetailedMetadataPayload.rationale: Provides full statutory lineage and audit evidence without bloating the map streaming pipeline

cdnUnavailable.behavior: Mobile falls back to local disk cache (Expo FileSystem / SQLite); if uncached, displays offline banner and bundled national overview ('IN'). Never substitutes mismatched tiles.

apiUnavailable.behavior: Map rendering continues seamlessly using cached tiles. Interactive point inspection ('locate') displays 'Service temporarily unavailable' without crashing the map canvas.

databaseUnavailable.behavior: Static tiles and cached API responses continue serving from edge CDN and Redis. Dynamic writes/queries fail gracefully with HTTP 503 DATABASE_FAILURE.

tileUnavailable.behavior: MapLibre leaves unretrievable tile blank with retry affordance. Never stretches adjacent tiles or substitutes adjacent regions.

geometryVersionUnavailable.behavior: Returns HTTP 404 NOT_FOUND with explicit error code. Never substitutes a different temporal version silently.
